This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The light-theme message-length hint changes from 70% to 30% lightness, making a secondary counter visually dominant on every mobile flag modal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in mobile/modal.scss line 102 that the color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. For light themes, this changes from 70% lightness to 30% lightness, which is a significant darkening that makes the text much more prominent/darker than before. This appears to be an error - the pattern used elsewhere in the diff typically keeps similar lightness values (e.g., 50%/50%, 70%/30% where primary gets lighter and secondary gets darker). Here the light theme value went from 70% to 30%, which is the opposite direction and inconsistent with the rest of the changes.

This is inconsistent with similar changes elsewhere in the codebase where the light-theme value is preserved (e.g., in desktop/topic-post.scss line 318 which keeps 20% for light theme). This appears to be an unintentional contrast reduction that could affect readability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss:48 — Inlining the same theme-aware scaling formula across 109 declarations duplicates palette policy and makes future changes another error-prone cross-file sweep

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff introduces the same `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: Y%))` pattern across many files (109 declarations as claimed). This is a legitimate maintainability concern - the same formula is copy-pasted throughout the codebase rather than being abstracted into a reusable mixin or variable. This makes future theme changes error-prone and increases maintenance burden. The finding is grounded in the actual diff content showing repetitive patterns across multiple SCSS files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — No compiled-CSS regression test covers both theme branches, allowing this light-theme value to change from 30% to 70% even though only dark themes should change

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 291 in desktop/topic-post.scss, the diff shows the change from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The finding claims the light-theme value changed from 30% to 70%, but this is actually intentional - the dark-light-choose function takes (light-theme-value, dark-theme-value) as arguments. The 70% lightness on $primary for light themes and 30% lightness on $secondary for dark themes is the intended behavior pattern seen throughout this diff. The finding misunderstands the purpose of the change and incorrectly frames a deliberate design decision as a regression. The claim about missing CSS regression tests is speculative and not verifiable from the diff.
